items.stem: Briefly explain why (f ∘ g)(x) is generally not equal to (g ∘ f)(x).
items.answer: The order of operations matters: f(g(x)) applies g first, g(f(x)) applies f first; e.g. doubling then adding 3 differs from adding 3 then doubling.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: The order of operations matters: f(g(x)) applies g first, g(f(x)) applies f first; e.g. doubling then adding 3 differs from adding 3 then doubling. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: For f(x) = -2x − 1 and g(x) = x² + 6, find expressions for (f ∘ g)(x) and (g ∘ f)(x), and use them to explain why composition is not commutative.
items.markingKey: (f∘g)(x) = -2(x² + 6) − 1 = -2x² − 13 (A1); (g∘f)(x) = (-2x − 1)² + 6 (A1); R1 e.g. at x = 1 they give −15 and 15, which differ.

items.stem: "(f ∘ g)(x) means f(x) × g(x)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: It means f applied to g(x), i.e. substituting g(x) into f; the product is written (fg)(x).
items.markingKey: It means f applied to g(x), i.e. substituting g(x) into f; the product is written (fg)(x). 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "A logistic population eventually exceeds its carrying capacity because it never stops growing." Explain the flaw in this statement.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "logarithmic model"?
options: Given by f(x) = a + b ln x, x > 0, describing quantities that keep increasing but ever more slowly
A graph of log y against x; data following y = abˣ lie on a straight line with gradient log b and intercept log a
The upper limit L that a logistic model approaches, e.g. the maximum population an environment can support
A function in which each output comes from exactly one input, so that an inverse function exists
items.answer: Given by f(x) = a + b ln x, x > 0, describing quantities that keep increasing but ever more slowly
items.markingKey: A. "logarithmic model" is given by f(x) = a + b ln x, x > 0, describing quantities that keep increasing but ever more slowly.

items.stem: Define the term "one-to-one function".
items.answer: A function in which each output comes from exactly one input, so that an inverse function exists

items.stem: Data on the cost of a project (y thousand EUR) and its size (x hundred m²) are (x, y): (1, 5.94); (3, 10); (5, 13.4); (6, 14.9); (8, 17.2); (15, 23.5). items.stem: The number of fish in a lake t years after observations began is modelled by N(t) = 10000/(1 + 9.9e^(−0.41t)). Explain what happens to N(t) as t becomes large and interpret this in context.
items.markingKey: R1 e^(−0.41t) → 0, so N → 10000/1 = 10000; R1 10000 is the carrying capacity – the maximum number the environment/population can sustain.

items.stem: For f(x) = 4x + 4 and g(x) = −x² − 2, find expressions for (f ∘ g)(x) and (g ∘ f)(x), and use them to explain why composition is not commutative.
items.markingKey: (f∘g)(x) = 4(−x² − 2) + 4 = -4x² − 4 (A1); (g∘f)(x) = −(4x + 4)² − 2 (A1); R1 e.g. at x = 1 they give −8 and −66, which differ.

items.stem: Isabel writes: "The graph of y = 3f(x) is the graph of y = f(x) stretched horizontally by factor 3." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Multiplying outside the function stretches vertically: y-coordinates are tripled, x-coordinates unchanged.
items.markingKey: Multiplying outside the function stretches vertically: y-coordinates are tripled, x-coordinates unchanged. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.
